label: text
text: The annual meeting of the Hongkong Boxing Association is to be held on Thursday next.

label: text
text: After buying a quart bottle of stout for his supper a man broke the seal on the bottle and drew off a glassful of the stout, which he drank with enjoyment. When he was pouring out a second glass out bobbed the head of a snake. He took the bottle and the snake to the local sanitary office, where it was found to be a grass snake 15 inches long.

label: text
text: The shop window displays of certain Bradford drapers in connection with Shopping Week, offended the susceptibilities of Bradford Diocesan Lay Readers' Association, who passed a resolution that the displays have a tendency towards indecency and have decided to draw the attention of the chief constable to the matter. The displays to which objection is taken are those of wax models of girls exhibiting lingerie. The drapers concerned strongly resent this criticism, and point out that they have to display lingerie as it is a part of women's attire.

label: text
text: Messrs. Vernon and Smyth in their share reported dated October 30, comment as follows: —Since the boycott and strike in the Colony and the stoppage of credit, the Stock Exchange has been closed since June 22 and reopened on 21st inst. With the exception of "Banks" and "Insurances" which show a slight drop in prices, all other stocks almost without exception show a capital depreciation of between 30 per cent. and 40 per cent.; and in some cases as much as 50 per cent.; with the exchange closed there was small enquiry for investment Shares at bargain prices but with the re-opening this enquiry appears to have ceased, and the market closes practically without buyers or sellers. Calls and New Issues on several stocks could not be met and the dates have had to be postponed.

label: text
text: The court-martial of the officers and soldiers who were implicated in the April military rising at Lisbon ended in an absolvatory sentence, the generals who formed the jury deciding after five hours' deliberation that it had been proved that the revolt had been inspired by patriotic motives. Exceptional interest was attached to the court-martial throughout the country, owing to the high moral and military status of the accused, some of whom rendered distinguished service in the war. The sentence was received with public approval.

label: text
text: The floating dock at Southampton has now lifted successfully all the biggest Atlantic liners except the "Leviathan".

label: text
text: Ships arriving with cargo at Hamburg during the first half of the year represented a million-and-half tons more than in the corresponding period of 1913.

label: text
text: Col. J. Obed Smith, Commissioner of Immigration in London for many years for the Dominion, on a trans-Canada tour, expressed the view that the Government should undertake the work of finding new markets for the grain products of Canada. Colonel Smith made the suggestion that it would be a good thing to distribute millions of loaves of wheat bread in China to accustom the Chinese to eating white bread. Mr. Smith predicted that if proper steps were taken to enlarge the Oriental market, it would within 10 years absorb a large percentage of the wheat grown on the prairies.

label: text
text: Ireland owns more than 50,000 cottages erected at the expense of the local authorities, to provide housing for labourers. The policy of their erection dates from as far back as 1883 when T. P. O'Connor secured enactment of a bill for that purpose by the British Parliament, and it has since been largely extended. The rent of one of these cottages in the Cork rural district is only 42 cents a week.

label: text
text: A series of Bible Studies will be given at the Helena May Institute on Fridays at 11 a.m. conducted by Rev. W. R. Robb. All women are invited.

label: text
text: March next year is the date given for the completion of the 7,600-ton cruiser "Enterprise," which was laid down in June 1918.

text: St. Andrew's Society, Penang, will observe St. Andrew's Day on November 27 by a dinner and ball at the E. and O. Hotel.

label: text
text: Money is literally being poured into Britain from the States for the purpose of starting a big Prohibition campaign. A number of M.P.S. are being "got at" quietly, and the thin edge of the wedge will become apparent when the question of "local option" is again raised. Mr. Scrymgeour threatens with the commencement of a national drought (alcoholically speaking) in 1927.

label: text
text: It is calculated that the number of men now employed in private shipbuilding yards on warship work is no more than a fifth of the pre-war number.

label: text
text: The presidency of the French Cabinet has issued this note: "Premier Painlevé has received a letter from the manager of the Ford automobile plant in France announcing that the Ford company is subscribing for 1,000,000 francs of the French 4 per cent. gold loan." At the present exchange rate 1,000,000 francs is equivalent to a little more than $47,000 (g).

label: text
text: The Committee of Imperial Defence has decided that the defence of the Suez Canal requires naval patrols, troops on the banks, and at least 12,000 troops at Cairo.

text: Polish policemen are being taught foreign languages. Those proficient in other tongues besides their own wear on their arm the first letter of the name of the other language spoken.

The miners' representatives who called on the Prime Minister in regard to the dispute as to their wages were quite pleased with the visit. Mr. Baldwin is the most accessible and the most courteous of Premiers, and in spite of the political chasm between them the Labour members cannot help liking him. "I hate Baldwin's speeches," one of them said, "he cuts the wind out of my sails!"
The Earl of Oxford and Asquith has accepted an invitation to become a Freeman of Huddersfield. His mother was daughter of Mr. William Williams; of Huddersfield, and part of his education was received at Huddersfield College. When he visits Huddersfield on Friday, November 6, the Earl will address a big Liberal demonstration and speak at the local Congregational Church Centenary celebration.

Mr. Hugh Fraser, of the Manila Electric Company, has returned from a round-the-world trip which began last April. He has visited Italy, France, Holland, England and Scotland. He said that he found business very bad in Europe but very good in the United States.
Word has been received in Manila telling of the death of Miss M. C. Tuohy, sister of A. R. Tuohy, business manager and director of advertising for the "Daily Bulletin." Miss Tuohy, whose death occurred in San Francisco, had been in ill health for some time and her condition became serious recently when she suffered severely from a fall down stairs at her home.

Mr. Edwin Potter, vice president of the Guaranty Trust Company of New York, and Mrs. Potter have gone to Manila for a month's stay. With them are Mr. and Mrs. C. M. Marvin, the former assistant vice-president of the Guaranty Trust Company. They will stop at the Manila Hotel, afterward, continuing round the world. The Guaranty Trust Company has banks in Europe, but none in the Orient. Mr. Potter said that he had gone to Manila on business, but refused to go into details.
